"""Offline tests for the CI gate checkers (scripts/*.py).

These tests exercise the checker *logic* deterministically: they do not run a
real mypy or pip-audit scan against the network. They prove that the checkers
(and their CI wiring contract) fail closed. Actual scans are separate jobs whose
results are reported by CI.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
SCRIPTS = ROOT / "scripts"


def _load(name: str):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, SCRIPTS / f"{name}.py")
    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    assert spec.loader is not None
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
    return mod


def _run(script: str, *args: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    return subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, str(SCRIPTS / f"{script}.py"), *args],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        cwd=ROOT,
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Schema gate
SCHEMA = ROOT / "docs/req/req-schema.json"
REGISTRY = ROOT / "docs/req/requirements.yaml"


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_schema_valid_registry_passes():
    assert _run("validate_requirements", "--registry", str(REGISTRY), "--schema", str(SCHEMA)).returncode == 0


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_schema_missing_file_fails(tmp_path):
    r = _run("validate_requirements", "--registry", str(tmp_path / "nope.yaml"), "--schema", str(SCHEMA))
    assert r.returncode == 1
    assert "not found" in r.stderr


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_schema_malformed_yaml_fails(tmp_path):
    bad = tmp_path / "bad.yaml"
    bad.write_text("registry_version: x\n  broken: [\n")
    r = _run("validate_requirements", "--registry", str(bad), "--schema", str(SCHEMA))
    assert r.returncode == 1
    assert "malformed YAML" in r.stderr


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_schema_duplicate_key_fails(tmp_path):
    dup = tmp_path / "dup.yaml"
    dup.write_text('registry_version: "a"\nregistry_version: "b"\n')
    r = _run("validate_requirements", "--registry", str(dup), "--schema", str(SCHEMA))
    assert r.returncode == 1
    assert "duplicate key" in r.stderr.lower()


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_schema_violation_fails(tmp_path):
    import yaml

    reg = yaml.safe_load(REGISTRY.read_text())
    reg["requirements"][0]["priority"] = "Critical"  # not in MoSCoW enum
    bad = tmp_path / "viol.yaml"
    bad.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(reg, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True))
    r = _run("validate_requirements", "--registry", str(bad), "--schema", str(SCHEMA))
    assert r.returncode == 1
    assert "requirements/0" in r.stderr


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_schema_duplicate_ids_fail(tmp_path):
    import copy

    import yaml

    reg = yaml.safe_load(REGISTRY.read_text())
    reg["requirements"].append(copy.deepcopy(reg["requirements"][0]))  # duplicate first id
    bad = tmp_path / "dupid.yaml"
    bad.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(reg, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True))
    r = _run("validate_requirements", "--registry", str(bad), "--schema", str(SCHEMA))
    assert r.returncode == 1
    assert "duplicate requirement id" in r.stderr


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- AI-use gate
@pytest.mark.unit
def test_ai_use_no_log_change_fails():
    import tempfile
    from pathlib import Path as P

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        root = P(d)
        (root / "docs").mkdir()
        (root / "docs/x.py").write_text("x=1\n")
        mod = _load("check_ai_use_log")
        errs = mod.check(["docs/x.py"], root)
    assert errs and "no AI-use log change" in errs[0]


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_ai_use_bare_pr_url_insufficient():
    import tempfile
    from pathlib import Path as P

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        root = P(d)
        (root / "transcripts").mkdir()
        log = root / "transcripts/O5-AI-Use-Log.md"
        log.write_text(
            "# log\nTask: O5. Scope: selector. Commit: abc123.\n"
            "See https://github.com/Caicys297/TradingAgents-CS5351/pull/29\n"
        )
        mod = _load("check_ai_use_log")
        errs = mod.check(["transcripts/O5-AI-Use-Log.md"], root)
    assert errs and "no real session" in errs[0]


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_ai_use_absolute_path_rejected():
    import tempfile
    from pathlib import Path as P

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        root = P(d)
        (root / "transcripts").mkdir()
        log = root / "transcripts/O5-AI-Use-Log.md"
        log.write_text("Task: t. Scope: s. Commit: abc.\nSession: https://x/s/1\nLocal: /Users/me/secret\n")
        mod = _load("check_ai_use_log")
        errs = mod.check(["transcripts/O5-AI-Use-Log.md"], root)
    assert any("absolute path" in e for e in errs)


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_ai_use_valid_session_url_passes():
    import tempfile
    from pathlib import Path as P

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        root = P(d)
        (root / "transcripts").mkdir()
        log = root / "transcripts/O5-AI-Use-Log.md"
        log.write_text(
            "Task: O5. Usage scope: selector. Implementation commit: abc123.\n"
            "Session export: https://opencode.example/session/xyz\n"
        )
        mod = _load("check_ai_use_log")
        errs = mod.check(["transcripts/O5-AI-Use-Log.md"], root)
    assert errs == []


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_ai_use_missing_marker_fails():
    import tempfile
    from pathlib import Path as P

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        root = P(d)
        (root / "transcripts").mkdir()
        log = root / "transcripts/O5-AI-Use-Log.md"
        log.write_text("Session: https://x/s/1\n")  # no task/scope/commit
        mod = _load("check_ai_use_log")
        errs = mod.check(["transcripts/O5-AI-Use-Log.md"], root)
    assert any("association marker" in e for e in errs)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Type checker
@pytest.mark.unit
def test_typecheck_identity_is_per_diagnostic():
    mod = _load("typecheck")
    lines = [
        "cli/run.py:188: error: Cannot assign to a method  [method-assign]",
        "cli/run.py:200: error: Other thing  [method-assign]",
    ]
    ids = mod.identities(lines)
    assert len(ids) == 2 and ids[0] != ids[1]  # same file+code, distinct diagnostics


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_typecheck_new_diagnostic_blocks_regardless_of_removals():
    mod = _load("typecheck")
    base = {"a.py:arg-type:deadbeef"}
    current_new = ["a.py:return-value:cafef00d"]
    new = set(current_new) - base
    assert new  # a brand-new diagnostic is blocking


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Dep audit
@pytest.mark.unit
def test_dep_audit_new_vuln_blocks():
    mod = _load("dep_audit")
    report = {"dependencies": [{"name": "foo", "version": "1.0",
                                "vulns": [{"id": "GHSA-xxxx", "fix_versions": ["1.2"]}]}]}
    found = mod.findings(report)
    new = [(p, v, vid, f) for (p, v, vid, f) in found if (p, vid) not in mod.baseline_keys({})]
    assert new == [("foo", "1.0", "GHSA-xxxx", "1.2")]


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_dep_audit_scanner_failure_is_not_clean(monkeypatch):
    mod = _load("dep_audit")

    class _Proc:
        returncode = 2
        stdout = ""
        stderr = "network error"

    monkeypatch.setattr(mod.subprocess, "run", lambda *a, **k: _Proc())
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc:
        mod.run_pip_audit()
    assert exc.value.code == 2  # failure, never treated as clean


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_dep_audit_bad_json_is_scanner_failure(monkeypatch):
    mod = _load("dep_audit")

    class _Proc:
        returncode = 1
        stdout = "not json"
        stderr = ""

    monkeypatch.setattr(mod.subprocess, "run", lambda *a, **k: _Proc())
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc:
        mod.run_pip_audit()
    assert exc.value.code == 2

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Type checker
@pytest.mark.unit
def test_typecheck_identity_is_per_diagnostic():
    mod = _load("typecheck")
    lines = [
        "cli/run.py:188: error: Cannot assign to a method  [method-assign]",
        "cli/run.py:200: error: Other thing  [method-assign]",
    ]
    ids = mod.identities(lines)
    assert len(ids) == 2 and ids[0] != ids[1]  # same file+code, distinct diagnostics


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_typecheck_blocks_new_diagnostic_via_baseline_diff(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    """A new identity absent from the baseline is reported as blocking."""
    mod = _load("typecheck")
    baseline = tmp_path / "mypy-baseline.txt"
    baseline.write_text("# baseline\ncli/run.py:method-assign:deadbeef\n")
    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "BASELINE", baseline)
    # Simulate mypy emitting one baseline diagnostic + one brand-new diagnostic.
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        mod,
        "run_mypy",
        lambda: [
            "cli/run.py:188: error: Cannot assign to a method  [method-assign]",
            "tradingagents/agents/new.py:9: error: Incompatible types  [assignment]",
        ],
    )
    # Force the baseline identity to match the first emitted line.
    first_id = mod.identities(
        ["cli/run.py:188: error: Cannot assign to a method  [method-assign]"]
    )[0]
    baseline.write_text(f"# baseline\n{first_id}\n")
    rc = mod.main([])
    assert rc == 1  # the second (new) diagnostic blocks


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_typecheck_removal_does_not_mask_new(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    """Deleting baseline errors must not allow a different new error through."""
    mod = _load("typecheck")
    baseline = tmp_path / "mypy-baseline.txt"
    baseline.write_text("# baseline\nold.py:arg-type:deadbeef\n")
    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "BASELINE", baseline)
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        mod,
        "run_mypy",
        lambda: ["new.py:return-value:cafef00d"],
    )
    assert mod.main([]) == 1

input.content:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, 'v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+']
  pull_request:

# Least privilege: never run untrusted PR code with write credentials.
permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  test:
    name: tests (py${{ matrix.python-version }}${{ matrix.tz && format(', {0}', matrix.tz) || '' }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.11", "3.12", "3.13", "3.14"]
        include:
          - python-version: "3.12"
            tz: America/New_York
    env:
      TZ: ${{ matrix.tz }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
      - name: Install (with dev extras)
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -e ".[dev]"
      - name: Run test suite
        run: pytest -v

  smoke-install:
    name: clean-install smoke
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Fresh install (no dev extras) and import
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install .
          python -c "import tradingagents, cli.main; print('clean-install import OK')"

  lint:
    name: ruff (strict, full repo)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Install ruff
        run: pip install "ruff>=0.16"
      - name: Lint the repository
        run: ruff check .

  requirements-schema:
    name: requirements schema
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Install validation deps
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install "PyYAML==6.0.3" "jsonschema==4.26.0"
      - name: Validate requirements registry
        run: python scripts/validate_requirements.py

  type-check:
    name: type check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Install (dev + pinned type tool)
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -e ".[dev]"
          pip install "mypy==1.18.2" "types-PyYAML==6.0.12.20250915"
      - name: Check for new type diagnostics vs trusted base baseline
        env:
          # Baseline is read from the merge-base (trusted), not from this PR's tree,
          # so a PR cannot widen its own allowances. On first introduction the job
          # bootstraps against THIS PR (A review required); see scripts/typecheck.py.
          GITHUB_BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
          GITHUB_EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: python scripts/typecheck.py

  dependency-audit:
    name: dependency audit
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Install (dev + pinned scanner) into the audited env
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -e ".[dev]"
          pip install "pip-audit==2.9.0"
      - name: Audit installed environment vs trusted base baseline
        env:
          GITHUB_BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
          GITHUB_EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: python scripts/dep_audit.py

  ai-use-log:
    name: ai-use log
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run mypy over the approved scope and fail on any *new* diagnostic.

Trust model (correction 1): the baseline is read from the **trusted base
revision** (``origin/<base>:ci/baselines/mypy-baseline.txt``), never from the
PR's own tree, so a PR cannot widen its allowances for its own new findings.
Bootstrap: if the baseline file does not exist on the base revision (first
introduction), the job uses the checked-in file from THIS PR and prints a clear
BOOTSTRAP notice — A must review that initial baseline.

Diagnostic identity (correction 2): ``file:code:msghash`` **with multiplicity**.
Identical diagnostics are tracked as a multiset (a count per identity), so two
identical errors in different functions do not collapse; removing an old error
never offsets introducing a new one.

mypy exit semantics (correction 2): exit 1 is normal "errors found", but the
process must have produced recognizable diagnostics. If mypy exits nonzero with
**no parseable diagnostics**, that is an execution failure (exit 2), not success.

Usage:
    python scripts/typecheck.py
    python scripts/typecheck.py --update     # human-only: rewrite the local baseline

Exit codes:
    0  no new diagnostics
    1  new diagnostic(s) beyond the trusted baseline
    2  mypy failed / produced output we could not parse
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

SCOPE = [
    "tradingagents/agents/evidence_gate.py",
    "tradingagents/agents/state.py",
    "tradingagents/graph",
    "cli/display.py",
    "cli/run.py",
    "scripts/validate_requirements.py",
    "scripts/check_ai_use_log.py",
    "scripts/typecheck.py",
    "scripts/dep_audit.py",
]

BASELINE = Path("ci/baselines/mypy-baseline.txt")

DIAG_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(?P<path>[^:\n]+):(?P<line>\d+)(?::(?P<col>\d+))?: error: (?P<msg>.*?)(?:  \[(?P<code>[a-z-]+)\])?$"
)


def _identity(m: re.Match) -> str:
    code = m.group("code") or "no-code"
    # Normalise line numbers/raw digits so a moved-but-identical error keeps its key;
    # include the message text so distinct errors in the same file+code stay distinct.
    norm = re.sub(r"\b\d+\b", "N", m.group("msg"))
    digest = hashlib.sha1(norm.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12]
    return f"{m.group('path')}:{code}:{digest}"


def parse(lines: list[str]) -> Counter:
    """Return a multiset (Counter) of diagnostic identities."""
    counts: Counter = Counter()
    for ln in lines:
        m = DIAG_RE.match(ln)
        if m:
            counts[_identity(m)] += 1
    return counts


def readable(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    return [ln for ln in lines if DIAG_RE.match(ln)]


def run_mypy() -> list[str]:
    cmd = [
        sys.executable, "-m", "mypy", *SCOPE,
        "--ignore-missing-imports",
        "--follow-imports=silent",
        "--show-error-codes",
        "--no-error-summary",
        "--no-incremental",
    ]
    proc = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    out = proc.stdout.splitlines()
    diags = readable(out)
    if proc.returncode not in (0, 1):
        print(proc.stdout, file=sys.stderr)
        print(proc.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
        raise SystemExit(2)
    # exit 1 with no parseable diagnostics is an execution problem, not success.
    if proc.returncode == 1 and not diags:
        print("ERROR: mypy exited 1 but produced no recognizable diagnostics:", file=sys.stderr)
        print(proc.stdout[-2000:], file=sys.stderr)
        print(proc.stderr[-2000:], file=sys.stderr)
        raise SystemExit(2)
    return out


def _load_baseline_text(base_ref: str) -> str | None:
    """Read the baseline from the trusted base revision; None if absent there."""
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "show", f"origin/{base_ref}:{BASELINE.as_posix()}"],
            capture_output=True, text=True,
        )
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        return None
    return proc.stdout


def load_baseline() -> tuple[Counter, str]:
    """Return (baseline multiset, source string) from the trusted base revision."""
    base_ref = os.environ.get("GITHUB_BASE_REF", "").strip()
    if os.environ.get("GITHUB_EVENT_NAME") == "pull_request" and base_ref:
        text = _load_baseline_text(base_ref)
        if text is not None:
            return parse(text.splitlines()), f"trusted base origin/{base_ref}"
        print(
            "BOOTSTRAP: baseline absent on base revision; using this PR's checked-in "
            "baseline. A must review this initial baseline before merge.",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
    if BASELINE.is_file():
        return parse(BASELINE.read_text().splitlines()), f"working tree {BASELINE}"
    return Counter(), "empty (no baseline)"


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--update", action="store_true", help="rewrite local baseline (human-only)")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    lines = run_mypy()
    current = parse(lines)

    if args.update:
        BASELINE.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        header = (
            "# mypy itemized baseline (file:code:msghash), one line per occurrence.\n"
            "# Trusted base revision supplies this to CI; regenerate with --update.\n"
        )
        rows: list[str] = []
        for ident, n in sorted(current.items()):
            rows.extend([ident] * n)
        BASELINE.write_text(header + "\n".join(rows) + ("\n" if rows else ""))
        print(f"baseline updated: {sum(current.values())} diagnostic occurrence(s)")
        return 0

    baseline, source = load_baseline()
    # Multiset difference: a new occurrence beyond the baseline count is blocking.
    new: Counter = Counter()
    for ident, n in current.items():
        excess = n - baseline.get(ident, 0)
        if excess > 0:
            new[ident] = excess

    if new:
        total = sum(new.values())
        print(f"TYPECHECK FAILED: {total} new diagnostic occurrence(s) beyond baseline ({source}):", file=sys.stderr)
        # Report readable messages for the offending identities.
        remaining = Counter(new)
        for ln in lines:
            m = DIAG_RE.match(ln)
            if not m:
                continue
            ident = _identity(m)
            if remaining.get(ident, 0) > 0:
                print(f"  {ln}", file=sys.stderr)
                remaining[ident] -= 1
        return 1

    print(
        f"OK: no new type diagnostics (baseline source: {source}; "
        f"{sum(current.values())} current occurrence(s))"
    )
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Audit CI-installed dependencies and fail on newly introduced vulnerabilities.

Policy and honesty notes (corrections 1 & 4):
- The baseline is read from the **trusted base revision**
  (``origin/<base>:ci/baselines/pip-audit-baseline.json``), never from the PR tree,
  so a PR cannot widen its own allowances. Bootstrap uses the PR's file with a
  clear notice for A review.
- Scans the *actually installed* environment (direct + transitive).
- pip-audit's JSON does not carry severity. This checker therefore treats **every
  new finding as blocking** — a deliberately *conservative temporary* behavior,
  NOT verified severity-aware High/Critical classification. Adopting severity-aware
  blocking requires an additional authoritative source (e.g. OSV severity) and an
  owner decision; that is called out, not fabricated.
- Allowances are keyed by (package, id, affected-version); an allowance never
  silently covers a future affected version.
- Structural validation: a report that is not a well-formed pip-audit document
  (e.g. ``{}``) is a scanner failure (exit 2), never "clean". Skipped / unresolvable
  packages are reported. The local editable project is identified separately from
  unaudited third-party dependencies.

Usage:
    python scripts/dep_audit.py
    python scripts/dep_audit.py --update-baseline   # human-only

Exit codes:
    0  no new findings (and report structure valid)
    1  new finding(s) beyond the trusted baseline
    2  scanner failed / report invalid / could not validate
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

BASELINE = Path("ci/baselines/pip-audit-baseline.json")
VALID_APPROVAL = {"APPROVED", "ACCEPTED"}


class ScannerError(RuntimeError):
    pass


def run_pip_audit() -> dict:
    cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "pip_audit", "--format", "json", "--progress-spinner", "off"]
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
        raise ScannerError("pip-audit not installed") from exc
    if proc.returncode not in (0, 1):
        raise ScannerError(
            f"pip-audit failed (exit {proc.returncode}): {proc.stderr.strip()[:1500]}"
        )
    try:
        report = json.loads(proc.stdout)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
        raise ScannerError("pip-audit produced non-JSON output") from exc
    validate_report(report)
    return report


def validate_report(report: object) -> None:
    """Reject structurally-incomplete reports (e.g. ``{}``) as scanner failures."""
    if not isinstance(report, dict) or "dependencies" not in report:
        raise ScannerError("report has no 'dependencies' key (incomplete scan)")
    if not isinstance(report["dependencies"], list):
        raise ScannerError("report 'dependencies' is not a list")
    # pip-audit includes a 'skip_reason'/'skips' in some versions; capture if present.
    deps = report["dependencies"]
    if deps and not all(isinstance(d, dict) and "name" in d for d in deps):
        raise ScannerError("report dependency entries malformed")


def findings(report: dict) -> list[tuple[str, str, str, str]]:
    """(package, installed_version, vuln_id, fix)."""
    out: list[tuple[str, str, str, str]] = []
    for dep in report.get("dependencies", []):
        name = dep.get("name", "?")
        version = dep.get("version", "?")
        for vuln in dep.get("vulns", []) or []:
            vid = vuln.get("id", "?")
            fixes = vuln.get("fix_versions", []) or []
            out.append((name, version, vid, ",".join(fixes) if fixes else "no fix available"))
    return out


def skipped(report: dict) -> list[str]:
    out: list[str] = []
    for dep in report.get("dependencies", []):
        reason = dep.get("skip_reason")
        if reason:
            out.append(f"{dep.get('name','?')}=={dep.get('version','?')}: {reason}")
    return out


def local_editable(report: dict) -> list[str]:
    """Identify this project's own editable install (not third-party)."""
    names: list[str] = []
    for dep in report.get("dependencies", []):
        name = str(dep.get("name", "")).lower()
        if name in ("tradingagents",):
            names.append(f"{dep.get('name')}=={dep.get('version')}")
    return names


def _load_baseline() -> tuple[dict, str]:
    base_ref = os.environ.get("GITHUB_BASE_REF", "").strip()
    if os.environ.get("GITHUB_EVENT_NAME") == "pull_request" and base_ref:
        try:
            proc = subprocess.run(
                ["git", "show", f"origin/{base_ref}:{BASELINE.as_posix()}"],
                capture_output=True, text=True,
            )
        except FileNotFoundError:
            proc = None
        if proc is not None and proc.returncode == 0:
            return json.loads(proc.stdout), f"trusted base origin/{base_ref}"
        print(
            "BOOTSTRAP: dependency baseline absent on base revision; using this PR's "
            "checked-in baseline. A must review this initial baseline.",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
    if BASELINE.is_file():
        return json.loads(BASELINE.read_text()), f"working tree {BASELINE}"
    return {"findings": []}, "empty"


def baseline_keys(base: dict) -> set[tuple[str, str, str]]:
    keys: set[tuple[str, str, str]] = set()
    for entry in base.get("findings", []):
        pkg = entry.get("package", "")
        vid = entry.get("id", "")
        ver = entry.get("affected_version", entry.get("version", ""))
        keys.add((pkg, vid, ver))
    return keys


def validate_baseline(base: dict) -> list[str]:
    """Reject PENDING owners / unapproved exceptions in the baseline."""
    problems: list[str] = []
    for entry in base.get("findings", []):
        if entry.get("owner", "PENDING") == "PENDING":
            problems.append(f"baseline finding {entry.get('package')} {entry.get('id')} has no owner")
        if entry.get("status") and entry["status"] not in VALID_APPROVAL:
            problems.append(
                f"baseline finding {entry.get('package')} {entry.get('id')} status "
                f"{entry.get('status')!r} not approved"
            )
    return problems


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--update-baseline", action="store_true", help="rewrite baseline (human-only)")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    try:
        report = run_pip_audit()
    except ScannerError as exc:
        print(f"ERROR: dependency scan failed: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    found = findings(report)

    if args.update_baseline:
        BASELINE.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        doc = {
            "_policy": (
                "Existing findings; each requires owner + remediation + (for any "
                "exception) approved status. New findings block. PRs must not widen "
                "this file. Severity is not provided by pip-audit JSON; new findings "
                "block conservatively until an authoritative severity source is adopted."
            ),
            "scanned_packages": len(report.get("dependencies", [])),
            "findings": [
                {
                    "package": p, "affected_version": v, "id": vid,
                    "fix": fix, "owner": "PENDING", "status": "PENDING",
                }
                for (p, v, vid, fix) in found
            ],
        }
        BASELINE.write_text(json.dumps(doc, indent=2) + "\n")
        print(f"baseline updated: {len(found)} finding(s) from {len(report.get('dependencies', []))} packages")
        return 0

    base, source = _load_baseline()
    meta_problems = validate_baseline(base)
    if meta_problems:
        print("ERROR: baseline metadata invalid (owners/exceptions must be approved):", file=sys.stderr)
        for p in meta_problems:
            print(f"  - {p}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    base_keys = baseline_keys(base)
    new = [(p, v, vid, fix) for (p, v, vid, fix) in found if (p, vid, v) not in base_keys]

    skip = skipped(report)
    signed = local_editable(report)
    print(f"scanned packages: {len(report.get('dependencies', []))} (baseline source: {source})")
    if signed:
        print(f"local editable project (audited for version only): {', '.join(signed)}")
    if skip:
        print("skipped/unscannable packages (reported, not treated as clean):")
        for s in skip:
            print(f"  - {s}")

    if new:
        print(f"DEPENDENCY AUDIT FAILED: {len(new)} new finding(s) beyond baseline:", file=sys.stderr)
        for (p, v, vid, fix) in new:
            print(f"  - {p}=={v}  {vid}  fix={fix}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(
            "  NOTE: severity not supplied by pip-audit JSON; ALL new findings block "
            "(conservative temporary policy, not severity-aware). Adopt an authoritative "
            "severity source + owner decision to refine.",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 1

    print(f"OK: no new dependency findings ({len(found)} total)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Structural AI-use evidence check for a PR (corrections 3 & 5).

This verifies that a code/prompt PR adds a **meaningful new** AI-use entry that
associates task, usage scope, and implementation commit(s) with an explicitly
identified session/export reference. It does NOT establish truthfulness; humans
review authenticity and access.

Key rules:
- Inspects only the PR's **added/modified lines** (via the merge-base diff), so an
  unchanged historical entry plus a whitespace edit cannot pass.
- Rejects whitespace-only edits and reuse of unchanged historical entries.
- A generic HTTPS URL is not automatically a session reference. A real session/
  export reference must be an https URL whose path/query clearly denotes a session
  or export, OR a resolvable in-repo ``transcripts/`` export file. PR URLs
  (github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<n>) — especially with punctuation, comments,
  query strings, or fragments — are rejected as session evidence.
- Machine-specific absolute paths used *as the evidence reference* are rejected.
  A historical log mentioning a local path elsewhere is not itself rejected.
- Implementation commit association: an entry line naming a commit SHA is accepted
  structurally; whether that SHA exists and relates to this PR is reported as a
  hint for human review (the check does not require the log commit to contain its
  own final SHA).
- `--changed-from-file` reads a NUL-separated changed-file list, so filenames with
  spaces are handled safely and never interpolated into shell.

Usage:
    python scripts/check_ai_use_log.py --changed-file A [--changed-file B ...] [--root .]
    python scripts/check_ai_use_log.py --changed-from-file changed_files.z [--root .]

Exit codes:
    0  a valid, newly-added AI-use entry exists (or no code/prompt change)
    1  code/prompt change without valid newly-added AI-use evidence
    2  usage / internal error
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

LOG_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"ai[-_ ]?use", re.IGNORECASE)
REQUIRED_FIELD_LABELS = ("task", "scope", "commit")

# https session/export heuristic: path or query shows "session"/"export"/"transcript".
SESSION_URL_RE = re.compile(
    r"https://[^\s)]*(?:session|sessions|export|exports|transcript|transcripts)[^\s)]*",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
PR_URL_RE = re.compile(r"https://github\.com/[^/\s]+/[^/\s]+/pull/\d+", re.IGNORECASE)
TRANSCRIPT_REF_RE = re.compile(r"transcripts/[^\s)`'\"]+\.(?:md|json|jsonl|txt)")
COMMIT_SHA_RE = re.compile(r"\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b")
ABS_PATH_RE = re.compile(r"(?:^|[\s(\"'`])(?:/Users/|/home/|[A-Za-z]:\\)")

# File classes that make the gate applicable.
CODE_PREFIXES = (
    "tradingagents/", "cli/", "scripts/", "prompts/",
    ".github/workflows/", "test/", "tests/",
)


def _is_ai_use_log(path: str) -> bool:
    p = Path(path)
    return "transcripts" in p.parts and LOG_NAME_RE.search(p.name) is not None


def _applicable(changed: list[str]) -> bool:
    for f in changed:
        if f.startswith(CODE_PREFIXES) and not _is_ai_use_log(f):
            return True
    return False


def _added_lines(path: Path) -> list[str]:
    """Return only the lines this PR added to ``path`` (merge-base three-dot diff)."""
    base_ref = sys.argv and None  # placeholder; base resolved below
    return []


def added_lines(path: Path, base_ref: str) -> list[str]:
    """Added ('+') lines for ``path`` versus the merge base with origin/<base>."""
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "diff", "--unified=0", f"origin/{base_ref}...HEAD", "--", path.as_posix()],
            capture_output=True, text=True,
        )
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return []
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        # If git diff is unavailable, fall back to the whole file (still validated).
        return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines()
    out: list[str] = []
    for ln in proc.stdout.splitlines():
        if ln.startswith("+") and not ln.startswith("+++"):
            out.append(ln[1:])
    return out


def _validate_entry(text_lines: list[str], root: Path) -> list[str]:
    """Validate one log's added content. Returns problems (empty = valid)."""
    joined = "\n".join(text_lines)
    if not joined.strip():
        return ["no added content (whitespace-only or unchanged entry) — not valid evidence"]

    lowered = joined.lower()
    missing = [lbl for lbl in REQUIRED_FIELD_LABELS if lbl not in lowered]
    if missing:
        return [f"missing field label(s): {', '.join(missing)}"]

    problems: list[str] = []

    session_urls = SESSION_URL_RE.findall(joined)
    transcript_refs = [r for r in TRANSCRIPT_REF_RE.findall(joined)]
    resolvable_exports = [r for r in transcript_refs if (root / r).is_file()]

    if not session_urls and not resolvable_exports:
        # Distinguish "only a PR URL" and "bare URL" for a clearer message.
        if PR_URL_RE.search(joined):
            problems.append(
                "PR URL is not session evidence (need an explicitly identified "
                "session/export https link or a resolvable transcripts/ export file)"
            )
        else:
            problems.append(
                "no real session/export reference (need an https session/export link "
                "or a resolvable transcripts/ export file)"
            )

    # Absolute local path used as the evidence reference is rejected.
    if ABS_PATH_RE.search(joined):
        problems.append("evidence references a machine-specific absolute path (reviewers cannot access it)")

    # Commit association: structural only; note for humans.
    if not COMMIT_SHA_RE.search(joined):
        problems.append("no implementation commit SHA associated with the entry")

    return problems


def _changed_from_file(zpath: Path) -> list[str]:
    raw = zpath.read_bytes()
    parts = raw.split(b"\x00")
    return [p.decode("utf-8", errors="replace") for p in parts if p]


def check(changed: list[str], root: Path, base_ref: str) -> list[str]:
    if not _applicable(changed):
        return []  # no code/prompt change -> gate not applicable

    log_files = [f for f in changed if _is_ai_use_log(f)]
    if not log_files:
        return ["code/prompt change with no AI-use log change under transcripts/"]

    errors: list[str] = []
    any_valid = False
    for rel in log_files:
        path = root / rel
        if not path.is_file():
            errors.append(f"{rel}: listed as changed but not found")
            continue
        added = added_lines(path, base_ref) if base_ref else path.read_text(
            encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"
        ).splitlines()
        problems = _validate_entry(added, root)
        if problems:
            errors.extend(f"{rel}: {p}" for p in problems)
        else:
            any_valid = True

    if errors:
        return errors
    if not any_valid:
        return ["no valid newly-added AI-use entry found"]
    return []


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--changed-file", action="append", default=[], dest="changed")
    parser.add_argument("--changed-from-file", type=Path, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--root", default=".", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--base-ref", default=None)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    changed = list(args.changed)
    if args.changed_from_file:
        changed.extend(_changed_from_file(args.changed_from_file))

    if not changed:
        # Empty change set is not automatically a pass if a diff file was provided.
        if args.changed_from_file:
            print("OK: no changed files reported; AI-use gate not applicable")
            return 0
        print("ERROR: no --changed-file / --changed-from-file provided", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    import os

    base_ref = args.base_ref or os.environ.get("GITHUB_BASE_REF", "")

    try:
        errors = check(changed, args.root, base_ref)
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        print(f"ERROR: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    if errors:
        print(f"AI-use evidence INVALID: {len(errors)} problem(s):", file=sys.stderr)
        for err in errors:
            print(f"  - {err}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    print("OK: valid newly-added AI-use evidence found")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

parts.text: Typecheck regen didn't take effect — the recheck sees "9 new" though the file has 9. The cause: `--update` wrote the file but `parse()` of the baseline re-derives identities from its lines; the file lines ARE identities (`file:code:hash`), not mypy output lines, so `DIAG_RE` doesn't match them → baseline parses as empty. Baseline format is identity lines, but `load_baseline`/`parse` expects mypy output. Fix: baseline loader should read identity lines directly (count), not `parse()`.

"""Offline tests for the corrected CI gate checkers (scripts/*.py).

Deterministic: no real mypy/pip-audit network scan. They prove the checkers fail
closed and enforce the corrected policies (trusted-base baselines, per-diagnostic
multiplicity, structural dependency-report validation, genuine new AI-use entry).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
SCRIPTS = ROOT / "scripts"


def _load(name: str):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, SCRIPTS / f"{name}.py")
    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    assert spec.loader is not None
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
    return mod


def _run(script: str, *args: str, env: dict | None = None) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    import os

    e = dict(os.environ)
    if env:
        e.update(env)
    return subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, str(SCRIPTS / f"{script}.py"), *args],
        capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=ROOT, env=e,
    )


# ============================================================ Schema gate
SCHEMA = ROOT / "docs/req/req-schema.json"
REGISTRY = ROOT / "docs/req/requirements.yaml"


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_schema_valid_registry_passes():
    assert _run("validate_requirements", "--registry", str(REGISTRY), "--schema", str(SCHEMA)).returncode == 0


@pytest.mark.unit
@pytest.mark.parametrize("content,needle", [
    ("registry_version: x\n  broken: [\n", "malformed YAML"),
    ('registry_version: "a"\nregistry_version: "b"\n', "duplicate key"),
])
def test_schema_bad_yaml_fails(tmp_path, content, needle):
    bad = tmp_path / "bad.yaml"
    bad.write_text(content)
    r = _run("validate_requirements", "--registry", str(bad), "--schema", str(SCHEMA))
    assert r.returncode == 1 and needle in r.stderr.lower()


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_schema_missing_file_fails(tmp_path):
    r = _run("validate_requirements", "--registry", str(tmp_path / "nope.yaml"), "--schema", str(SCHEMA))
    assert r.returncode == 1 and "not found" in r.stderr


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_schema_violation_and_dup_ids_fail(tmp_path):
    import copy

    import yaml

    reg = yaml.safe_load(REGISTRY.read_text())
    reg["requirements"][0]["priority"] = "Critical"
    bad = tmp_path / "v.yaml"
    bad.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(reg, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True))
    assert _run("validate_requirements", "--registry", str(bad), "--schema", str(SCHEMA)).returncode == 1

    reg2 = copy.deepcopy(yaml.safe_load(REGISTRY.read_text()))
    reg2["requirements"].append(copy.deepcopy(reg2["requirements"][0]))
    bad2 = tmp_path / "d.yaml"
    bad2.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(reg2, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True))
    r2 = _run("validate_requirements", "--registry", str(bad2), "--schema", str(SCHEMA))
    assert r2.returncode == 1 and "duplicate requirement id" in r2.stderr


# ============================================================ Type checker
def _mk_baseline(tmp: Path, identities: list[str]) -> Path:
    b = tmp / "mypy-baseline.txt"
    b.write_text("# baseline\n" + "\n".join(identities) + "\n")
    return b


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_typecheck_identity_distinct_for_same_code_different_message():
    mod = _load("typecheck")
    lines = [
        "cli/run.py:10: error: Cannot assign to method A  [method-assign]",
        "cli/run.py:20: error: Cannot assign to method B  [method-assign]",
    ]
    ids = mod.identities(lines) if hasattr(mod, "identities") else list(mod.parse(lines))
    assert len(ids) == 2 and len(set(ids)) == 2


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_typecheck_multiplicity_two_identical_need_two_in_baseline(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    """Two identical diagnostics require a baseline count of 2; one is not enough."""
    mod = _load("typecheck")
    line = "cli/run.py:188: error: Cannot assign to a method  [method-assign]"
    ident = list(mod.parse([line]))[0]
    # baseline has only ONE occurrence; mypy yields TWO -> one new (blocking)
    b = _mk_baseline(tmp_path, [ident])
    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "BASELINE", b)
    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "_load_baseline_text", lambda ref: None)  # force working-tree path
    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "run_mypy", lambda: [line, line])
    # no PR env => uses working-tree baseline
    monkeypatch.delenv("GITHUB_EVENT_NAME", raising=False)
    assert mod.main([]) == 1


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_typecheck_removal_does_not_offset_new(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    mod = _load("typecheck")
    old = list(mod.parse(["old.py:1: error: Old issue  [arg-type]"]))[0]
    b = _mk_baseline(tmp_path, [old])
    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "BASELINE", b)
    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "_load_baseline_text", lambda ref: None)
    monkeypatch.delenv("GITHUB_EVENT_NAME", raising=False)
    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "run_mypy", lambda: ["new.py:1: error: New issue  [return-value]"])
    assert mod.main([]) == 1


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_typecheck_trusted_base_ignores_pr_widening(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    """A PR that widens its own baseline cannot authorize a new diagnostic."""
    mod = _load("typecheck")
    newline = "x.py:1: error: Brand new  [return-value]"
    ident = list(mod.parse([newline]))[0]
    # PR working-tree baseline WIDENED to include the new identity:
    b = _mk_baseline(tmp_path, [ident])
    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "BASELINE", b)
    # ...but the trusted base revision has an EMPTY baseline:
    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "_load_baseline_text", lambda ref: "# empty\n")
    monkeypatch.setenv("GITHUB_EVENT_NAME", "pull_request")
    monkeypatch.setenv("GITHUB_BASE_REF", "main")
    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "run_mypy", lambda: [newline])
    assert mod.main([]) == 1  # trusted base wins; new diagnostic blocks


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_typecheck_mypy_exit1_without_diagnostics_is_execution_failure(monkeypatch):
    mod = _load("typecheck")

    class _P:
        returncode = 1
        stdout = "mypy: internal error, no parseable diagnostics"
        stderr = ""

    monkeypatch.setattr(mod.subprocess, "run", lambda *a, **k: _P())
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc:
        mod.run_mypy()
    assert exc.value.code == 2  # never treated as success


# ============================================================ Dep audit
@pytest.mark.unit
def test_dep_audit_empty_json_report_is_scanner_failure(monkeypatch):
    mod = _load("dep_audit")

    class _P:
        returncode = 0
        stdout = "{}"
        stderr = ""

    monkeypatch.setattr(mod.subprocess, "run", lambda *a, **k: _P())
    with pytest.raises(mod.ScannerError):
        mod.run_pip_audit()


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_dep_audit_scanner_exit2_is_failure(monkeypatch):
    mod = _load("dep_audit")

    class _P:
        returncode = 2
        stdout = ""
        stderr = "network error"

    monkeypatch.setattr(mod.subprocess, "run", lambda *a, **k: _P())
    with pytest.raises(mod.ScannerError):
        mod.run_pip_audit()


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_dep_audit_new_finding_blocks_main(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    mod = _load("dep_audit")
    report = {"dependencies": [{"name": "foo", "version": "1.0",
                                "vulns": [{"id": "GHSA-x", "fix_versions": ["1.2"]}]}]}
    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "run_pip_audit", lambda: report)
    base = tmp_path / "b.json"
    base.write_text(json.dumps({"findings": []}))
    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "BASELINE", base)
    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "_load_baseline", lambda: ({"findings": []}, "test"))
    assert mod.main([]) == 1


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_dep_audit_allowance_is_version_specific(monkeypatch):
    """A baseline allowance for v1.0 must not cover a future affected version 2.0."""
    mod = _load("dep_audit")
    base = {"findings": [{"package": "foo", "id": "GHSA-x", "affected_version": "1.0"}]}
    keys = mod.baseline_keys(base)
    found = [("foo", "2.0", "GHSA-x", "no fix")]  # same id, different version
    new = [(p, v, vid, f) for (p, v, vid, f) in found if (p, vid, v) not in keys]
    assert new  # blocks: version differs


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_dep_audit_pending_baseline_metadata_rejected():
    mod = _load("dep_audit")
    base = {"findings": [{"package": "foo", "id": "GHSA-x", "affected_version": "1.0",
                          "owner": "PENDING", "status": "PENDING"}]}
    assert mod.validate_baseline(base)  # non-empty => invalid


# ============================================================ AI-use gate
@pytest.mark.unit
def test_ai_use_no_log_change_fails(tmp_path):
    mod = _load("check_ai_use_log")
    (tmp_path / "tradingagents").mkdir()
    errs = mod.check(["tradingagents/x.py"], tmp_path, base_ref="")
    assert errs and "no AI-use log change" in errs[0]


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_ai_use_not_applicable_for_docs_only(tmp_path):
    mod = _load("check_ai_use_log")
    assert mod.check(["docs/readme.md"], tmp_path, base_ref="") == []


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_ai_use_bare_pr_url_is_not_session(tmp_path):
    mod = _load("check_ai_use_log")
    (tmp_path / "transcripts").mkdir()
    log = tmp_path / "transcripts/O5-AI-Use-Log.md"
    log.write_text("Task: t. Scope: s. Commit: abc1234.\n"
                   "See https://github.com/Caicys297/TradingAgents-CS5351/pull/29\n")
    errs = mod.check(["transcripts/O5-AI-Use-Log.md"], tmp_path, base_ref="")
    assert any("PR URL is not session evidence" in e for e in errs)


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_ai_use_absolute_path_rejected(tmp_path):
    mod = _load("check_ai_use_log")
    (tmp_path / "transcripts").mkdir()
    log = tmp_path / "transcripts/O5-AI-Use-Log.md"
    log.write_text("Task: t. Scope: s. Commit: abc1234.\n"
                   "Session: https://x/session/1\nLocal: /Users/me/secret\n")
    errs = mod.check(["transcripts/O5-AI-Use-Log.md"], tmp_path, base_ref="")
    assert any("absolute path" in e for e in errs)


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_ai_use_whitespace_only_edit_fails(tmp_path):
    mod = _load("check_ai_use_log")
    (tmp_path / "transcripts").mkdir()
    log = tmp_path / "transcripts/O5-AI-Use-Log.md"
    log.write_text("   \n\n  \n")
    errs = mod.check(["transcripts/O5-AI-Use-Log.md"], tmp_path, base_ref="")
    assert any("whitespace-only" in e.lower() for e in errs)


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_ai_use_missing_commit_association_fails(tmp_path):
    mod = _load("check_ai_use_log")
    (tmp_path / "transcripts").mkdir()
    log = tmp_path / "transcripts/O5-AI-Use-Log.md"
    log.write_text("Task: t. Scope: s.\nSession: https://x/session/1\n")
    errs = mod.check(["transcripts/O5-AI-Use-Log.md"], tmp_path, base_ref="")
    assert any("commit" in e for e in errs)


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_ai_use_genuine_resolvable_export_passes(tmp_path):
    mod = _load("check_ai_use_log")
    (tmp_path / "transcripts").mkdir()
    (tmp_path / "transcripts/O5-session-export.md").write_text("raw\nexport\n")
    log = tmp_path / "transcripts/O5-AI-Use-Log.md"
    log.write_text("Task: t. Usage scope: s. Implementation commit: abc1234.\n"
                   "Evidence: transcripts/O5-session-export.md\n")
    errs = mod.check(["transcripts/O5-AI-Use-Log.md"], tmp_path, base_ref="")
    assert errs == []


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_ai_use_changed_from_file_handles_spaces(tmp_path):
    """--changed-from-file is NUL-separated so spaces in filenames are safe."""
    z = tmp_path / "changed.z"
    z.write_bytes(b"docs/a file.md\x00tradingagents/x.py\x00")
    mod = _load("check_ai_use_log")
    files = mod._changed_from_file(z)
    assert files == ["docs/a file.md", "tradingagents/x.py"]

def _identity(m: re.Match) -> str:

"""Structural AI-use evidence check for a PR (hardened per review).

Goals:
- Inspect only the PR's **added lines** vs the merge base; if the merge base /
  git diff cannot be resolved, return a distinct EXECUTION FAILURE (exit 3),
  never fall back to validating the whole file.
- Require a genuine new entry associating task, usage scope, and an actual
  implementation commit that exists in the repo, with an explicitly identified
  session/export reference. A baseline main SHA alone is not this PR's
  implementation association.
- Reject PR URLs even when their query/fragment contains "session"/"export".
- Reject machine-absolute-path evidence; a *summary* file is not a raw export and
  does not by itself satisfy the genuine-export requirement (see notes).
- Truthfulness/authenticity is a human responsibility; this only checks structure.

Usage:
    python scripts/check_ai_use_log.py --changed-from-file changed.z [--root .]
    python scripts/check_ai_use_log.py --changed-file A --changed-file B [--root .]

Exit codes:
    0  valid newly-added AI-use evidence (or gate not applicable)
    1  evidence invalid (missing/weak entry)
    2  usage / internal error
    3  execution failure: could not resolve merge base / git diff
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

LOG_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"ai[-_ ]?use", re.IGNORECASE)
REQUIRED_FIELD_LABELS = ("task", "scope", "commit")

# A PR URL — regardless of trailing query/fragment.
PR_URL_RE = re.compile(r"https://github\.com/[^/\s]+/[^/\s]+/pull/\d+(?:[?#][^\s]*)?", re.IGNORECASE)
# A genuine session/export https reference: the URL *path/authority* must denote a
# session/export; query/fragment alone does NOT count (see validation logic).
HTTPS_URL_RE = re.compile(r"https://[^\s)>\]]+", re.IGNORECASE)
TRANSCRIPT_REF_RE = re.compile(r"transcripts/[^\s)`'\"]+\.(?:md|json|jsonl|txt)")
COMMIT_SHA_RE = re.compile(r"\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b")
ABS_PATH_RE = re.compile(r"(?:^|[\s(\"'`])(?:/Users/|/home/|[A-Za-z]:\\)")

CODE_PREFIXES = (
    "tradingagents/", "cli/", "scripts/", "prompts/",
    ".github/workflows/", "test/", "tests/",
)


class DiffError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when the merge base / git diff cannot be resolved."""


def _is_ai_use_log(path: str) -> bool:
    p = Path(path)
    return "transcripts" in p.parts and LOG_NAME_RE.search(p.name) is not None


def _applicable(changed: list[str]) -> bool:
    return any(f.startswith(CODE_PREFIXES) and not _is_ai_use_log(f) for f in changed)


def added_lines(path: Path, base_ref: str) -> list[str]:
    """Added ('+') lines for ``path`` vs the merge base with origin/<base>.

    Raises DiffError if git/diff/base cannot be resolved — the caller turns that
    into a distinct execution failure (no whole-file fallback).
    """
    if not base_ref:
        raise DiffError("no base ref available to compute the PR diff")
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "diff", "--unified=0", f"origin/{base_ref}...HEAD", "--", path.as_posix()],
            capture_output=True, text=True,
        )
    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
        raise DiffError("git is not available to compute the PR diff") from exc
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        raise DiffError(
            f"git diff failed for origin/{base_ref}...HEAD (exit {proc.returncode}): "
            f"{proc.stderr.strip()[:300]}"
        )
    out: list[str] = []
    for ln in proc.stdout.splitlines():
        if ln.startswith("+") and not ln.startswith("+++"):
            out.append(ln[1:])
    return out


def _is_session_url(url: str) -> bool:
    """True only if the URL's path/authority (not just query/fragment) is a session/export."""
    if PR_URL_RE.match(url):
        return False  # a PR URL is never session evidence, even with ?session=...
    # Strip query and fragment; only the pre-'?'/'#' part counts.
    core = re.split(r"[?#]", url, maxsplit=1)[0]
    return re.search(r"(?:session|sessions|export|exports|transcript|transcripts)", core, re.IGNORECASE) is not None


def _commit_exists(sha: str, root: Path) -> bool:
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(root), "cat-file", "-e", f"{sha}^{{commit}}"],
            capture_output=True, text=True,
        )
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return False
    return proc.returncode == 0


def _commit_in_range(sha: str, base_ref: str, root: Path) -> bool:
    """Whether ``sha`` is reachable in the PR range origin/<base>..HEAD."""
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(root), "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", sha, "HEAD"],
            capture_output=True, text=True,
        )
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return False
    return proc.returncode == 0


def _validate_entry(text_lines: list[str], root: Path, base_ref: str) -> list[str]:
    joined = "\n".join(text_lines)
    if not joined.strip():
        return ["no added content (whitespace-only or unchanged entry) — not valid evidence"]

    lowered = joined.lower()
    missing = [lbl for lbl in REQUIRED_FIELD_LABELS if lbl not in lowered]
    if missing:
        return [f"missing field label(s): {', '.join(missing)}"]

    problems: list[str] = []

    # Genuine session/export reference: a non-PR https URL whose path denotes a
    # session/export, or a resolvable transcripts/ export file.
    session_urls = [u for u in HTTPS_URL_RE.findall(joined) if _is_session_url(u)]
    transcript_refs = list(TRANSCRIPT_REF_RE.findall(joined))
    resolvable_exports = [r for r in transcript_refs if (root / r).is_file()]

    if not session_urls and not resolvable_exports:
        if PR_URL_RE.search(joined):
            problems.append(
                "PR URL is not session evidence (query/fragment containing 'session' does "
                "not count; need a genuine session/export URL path or a resolvable export file)"
            )
        else:
            problems.append(
                "no genuine session/export reference (need an https session/export URL or a "
                "resolvable transcripts/ export file)"
            )

    if ABS_PATH_RE.search(joined):
        problems.append("evidence references a machine-specific absolute path (reviewers cannot access it)")

    # Implementation-commit association must be a REAL commit in this PR's range.
    if base_ref:
        shas = COMMIT_SHA_RE.findall(joined)
        real = [s for s in shas if _commit_exists(s, root)]
        in_range = [s for s in real if _commit_in_range(s, base_ref, root)]
        if not shas:
            problems.append("no implementation commit SHA associated with the entry")
        elif not real:
            problems.append(
                "commit SHA(s) in the entry do not exist in the repository "
                "(a baseline main SHA alone is not this PR's implementation association)"
            )
        elif not in_range:
            problems.append(
                "commit SHA(s) exist but are not part of this PR's implementation range "
                "(origin/base..HEAD)"
            )

    return problems


def _changed_from_file(zpath: Path) -> list[str]:
    raw = zpath.read_bytes()
    return [p.decode("utf-8", errors="replace") for p in raw.split(b"\x00") if p]


def check(changed: list[str], root: Path, base_ref: str) -> list[str]:
    if not _applicable(changed):
        return []
    log_files = [f for f in changed if _is_ai_use_log(f)]
    if not log_files:
        return ["code/prompt change with no AI-use log change under transcripts/"]

    errors: list[str] = []
    any_valid = False
    for rel in log_files:
        path = root / rel
        if not path.is_file():
            errors.append(f"{rel}: listed as changed but not found")
            continue
        added = added_lines(path, base_ref)  # raises DiffError (no fallback)
        problems = _validate_entry(added, root, base_ref)
        if problems:
            errors.extend(f"{rel}: {p}" for p in problems)
        else:
            any_valid = True

    if errors:
        return errors
    if not any_valid:
        return ["no valid newly-added AI-use entry found"]
    return []


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--changed-file", action="append", default=[], dest="changed")
    parser.add_argument("--changed-from-file", type=Path, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--root", default=".", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--base-ref", default=None)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    changed = list(args.changed)
    if args.changed_from_file:
        changed.extend(_changed_from_file(args.changed_from_file))

    if not changed:
        if args.changed_from_file:
            print("OK: no changed files reported; AI-use gate not applicable")
            return 0
        print("ERROR: no --changed-file / --changed-from-file provided", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    base_ref = args.base_ref or os.environ.get("GITHUB_BASE_REF", "")

    # If the gate applies to a code/prompt change, a resolvable base is mandatory.
    if _applicable(changed) and not base_ref:
        print(
            "ERROR: code/prompt change but no base ref to compute the PR diff "
            "(GITHUB_BASE_REF / --base-ref); refusing to validate the whole file.",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 3

    try:
        errors = check(changed, args.root, base_ref)
    except DiffError as exc:
        print(f"ERROR: cannot obtain PR diff: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 3
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        print(f"ERROR: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    if errors:
        print(f"AI-use evidence INVALID: {len(errors)} problem(s):", file=sys.stderr)
        for err in errors:
            print(f"  - {err}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    print("OK: valid newly-added AI-use evidence found")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# CI — AI-use log (six-gate consolidated batch)

Owner: Member F (CI). Records AI (OpenCode) use on the consolidated six-gate CI
batch, per REQ-GOV-06. The repository does not prescribe a fixed path or schema.

## Format notes

- Task: implement authorized CI gate checkers (Requirements Schema, AI-use
  structural check, type checking, dependency audit) plus deterministic O5
  semantic cases, in one consolidated PR.
- Usage scope: repository inspection, checker scripts, offline tests, CI workflow
  wiring, baselines. No production feature code changes.

## Entry (this PR)

- Task: six-gate CI checkers (schema, ai-use, type, dependency) + deterministic O5.
- Usage scope: scripts/, test/offline/, .github/workflows/, ci/baselines/, transcripts/.
- Implementation commit: associated with this PR's implementation commit(s) in the
  `origin/<base>..HEAD` range (see PR commit list). No self-SHA requirement.
- Session/export evidence: genuine sanitized OpenCode session export at
  `transcripts/CI-opencode-session-export.json`
  (sha256 `61dd03b4cf3d1cc155dd32fd77b3396ba5727e223a8839c67e1756d1eff7c922`,
  produced with `opencode export <session> --sanitize`; session-directory and title

"""Offline tests for the hardened CI gate checkers (scripts/*.py).

Deterministic: no real mypy/pip-audit network scan. They prove the checkers fail

from __future__ import annotations

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]

def _load(name: str):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, SCRIPTS / f"{name}.py")
    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    assert spec.loader is not None
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
    return mod


def _run(script: str, *args: str, env: dict | None = None) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    import os

    e = dict(os.environ)
    if env:
        e.update(env)
    return subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, str(SCRIPTS / f"{script}.py"), *args],
        capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=ROOT, env=e,
    )

parts.text: One test fails in CI but passed locally: `test_ai_use_no_base_for_code_change_is_exit3` returns 1, not 3. In CI, `GITHUB_BASE_REF` env is set (the job runs on a PR), so `base_ref` is non-empty → skips the exit-3 branch and proceeds to `check()` → returns 1 (no log). Locally my shell had no `GITHUB_BASE_REF`. The test must clear that env. Fix: `monkeypatch.delenv`.

s=s.replace('''def test_ai_use_no_base_for_code_change_is_exit3(tmp_path):
    mod = _load("check_ai_use_log")
    (tmp_path / "scripts").mkdir()
    assert mod.main(["--changed-file", "scripts/x.py", "--root", str(tmp_path)]) == 3''',
'''def test_ai_use_no_base_for_code_change_is_exit3(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    mod = _load("check_ai_use_log")
    monkeypatch.delenv("GITHUB_BASE_REF", raising=False)
    monkeypatch.delenv("GITHUB_EVENT_NAME", raising=False)
    (tmp_path / "scripts").mkdir()
    assert mod.main(["--changed-file", "scripts/x.py", "--root", str(tmp_path)]) == 3''')
open(p,"w").write(s); print("fixed env isolation")

# PR #30 — Reviewer Evidence Index (final)

**Prepared:** 2026-11-20 (read-only evidence preparation)
**PR:** https://github.com/Caicys297/TradingAgents-CS5351/pull/30
**Current PR HEAD:** `e085bfd9699375345f914327fe584e1d27bde4c8`
**Base:** `99612ca64445ec650b9a5f42203fa166783800b1`
**CI run (current, all 11 success):** https://github.com/Caicys297/TradingAgents-CS5351/actions/runs/44728755857
**Review state:** No formal A review yet (only F's self-check comment; `reviewDecision=REVIEW_REQUIRED`).

> Facts below were re-verified at HEAD `e085bfd` (worktree) and the CI run above. Historical local run numbers are labelled as such.

## Evidence levels — kept strictly separate
1. **Observed checker nonzero exit** — demonstrated by executing the checker (subprocess or via pytest unit test). This is real local execution.
2. **Workflow configuration propagates an exit to job failure** — a `run:` step that exits nonzero fails the job because GitHub Actions runs each `run:` step with `bash -e` (non-`continue-on-error`). This is a *configuration fact*, not an observed event for the failure path.
3. **Actually observed failing remote job** — **NONE** for any checker's failure path. All remote jobs are green; no deliberately failing remote run exists (none was created).
4. **Required-check merge prevention** — **NOT VERIFIED.** Requires A/admin to set required checks and record a blocked-merge trial. Local runs and green CI do not prove this.

## Per-check evidence

### 1. Requirements Schema — job `requirements schema`
- **Command:** `python scripts/validate_requirements.py` (deps `PyYAML==6.0.3`, `jsonschema==4.26.0`).
- **Entry point:** `scripts/validate_requirements.py` → `validate()`.
- **Exit:** `1` on missing file / malformed YAML / duplicate YAML keys / schema violation / duplicate requirement IDs; `2` on missing dependency.
- **Verification method (accurate):**
  - `test_schema_valid_registry_passes`, `test_schema_missing_file_fails`, `test_schema_bad_yaml_fails` (param: malformed YAML **and** duplicate key), `test_schema_violation_and_dup_ids_fail` — these **create real invalid files in a tmp dir and invoke the validator as a real subprocess** (`subprocess.run` of the script), asserting the real return code. **Not mocked.**
- **Real execution:** green remote job (level 1 positive path); negative paths are real local subprocess executions (level 1), not remote.

### 2. AI-use — job `ai-use log`
- **Command:** `python scripts/check_ai_use_log.py --changed-from-file changed_files.z` (changed list produced by `git diff --name-only -z origin/<base>...HEAD`).
- **Entry point:** `scripts/check_ai_use_log.py` → `check()` / `_validate_entry()` / `_commit_in_range()`.
- **Exit:** `3` on diff/base resolution failure; `1` on weak/missing evidence; `2` usage error.
- **Verification method (accurate):**
  - **Real temporary Git histories** (genuine `git init/commit/update-ref`, real `git` subprocess): `test_commit_in_range_rejects_base_sha`, `test_commit_in_range_rejects_unrelated_sha`, `test_commit_in_range_accepts_pr_impl_sha`, `test_commit_in_range_accepts_earlier_impl_from_followup`.
  - **Real files, pure logic** (no git): `test_export_empty_json_rejected`, `test_export_metadata_only_rejected`, `test_export_messages_parts_accepted`, `test_export_authored_summary_md_rejected`, `test_ai_use_*`.
  - **Mocked subprocess:** `test_ai_use_diff_failure_raises` (mocks `subprocess.run` → git failure → `DiffError`); `test_ai_use_no_base_for_code_change_is_exit3` (no git call).
- **Real execution:** green remote job; CI log at HEAD shows `OK: valid newly-added AI-use evidence found` (13 changed files).

### 3. Type check — job `type check`
- **Command:** `python scripts/typecheck.py` (mypy `1.18.2`, `types-PyYAML==6.0.12.20250915`).
- **Entry point:** `scripts/typecheck.py` → `run_mypy()`, `load_baseline()`, `parse()`, `_commit_in_range`-analogue baseline read.
- **Exit:** `1` new diagnostic beyond baseline; `2` mypy execution failure (exit ∉ {0,1}, or exit 1 with no parseable diagnostics) or base-resolution failure; BOOTSTRAP (not an error) when base resolves but baseline genuinely absent.
- **Verification method (accurate):**
  - **Real mypy output parsing** (no subprocess mock): `test_typecheck_symbol_in_identity_distinct_functions`.
  - **Mocked `run_mypy`** (baseline-diff logic): `test_typecheck_same_total_move_between_functions_blocks`, `test_typecheck_multiplicity_two_identical_need_two_in_baseline`, `test_typecheck_removal_does_not_offset_new`, `test_typecheck_trusted_base_ignores_pr_widening`.

- **Real execution:** green remote job; CI log shows `BOOTSTRAP … genuinely absent on trusted base` then `OK: no new type diagnostics`.

### 4. Dependency audit — job `dependency audit`
- **Command:** `python scripts/dep_audit.py` (pip-audit `2.9.0`, on the CI-installed env via `pip install -e ".[dev]"`).
- **Entry point:** `scripts/dep_audit.py` → `run_pip_audit()`, `findings()`, `_load_baseline()`.

  - **Pure logic:** `test_dep_audit_allowance_version_specific`, `test_dep_audit_pending_metadata_rejected`.
- **Real execution:** green remote job; real pip-audit scan ran in CI.

- **Entry point (real production):** `tradingagents/dataflows/vendors/yahoo/news.get_global_news_yfinance` (via the integration test's adapter).
- **Nodes:** `test_s4_selected_path_filters_before_slice_and_keeps_fields`, `test_s4_t04d_filtered_to_zero_is_not_upstream_empty`, `test_s4_t04d_all_irrelevant_uses_the_all_irrelevant_enum_member`, `test_s4_filter_unavailable_text_is_distinct_from_filtered_empty`, `test_s3_zero_limit_skips_vendor`, `test_s3_empty_vendor_pool_is_distinct_from_filtered_pool` (the last is additional coverage; the relevant-success case is the primary one).

"""S3 adapter checks with fake Yahoo search and a per-test in-memory sink."""

import json
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from tradingagents.dataflows.errors import VendorUnavailableError
from tradingagents.dataflows.macro_news_filter import InvalidRequestError
from tradingagents.dataflows.vendors.yahoo import news


class MemorySink:
    def __init__(self):
        self.events = []

    def emit(self, event):
        self.events.append(event)


@pytest.fixture
def adapter(monkeypatch):
    sink = MemorySink()
    token = news._o5_evidence_sink.set(sink)
    monkeypatch.setattr(news, "get_config", lambda: {
        "global_news_lookback_days": 2,
        "global_news_article_limit": 10,
        "global_news_queries": ["q1", "q2", "q3"],
    })
    monkeypatch.setattr(news, "yf_retry", lambda fn: fn())
    yield sink
    news._o5_evidence_sink.reset(token)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("limit", [True, -1, 2.5])
def test_s3_invalid_limit_never_fetches(monkeypatch, adapter, limit):
    monkeypatch.setattr(news.yf, "Search", lambda **kwargs: pytest.fail("fetched"))
    with pytest.raises(InvalidRequestError) as error:
        news.get_global_news_yfinance("2026-09-28", limit=limit)
    assert error.value.field == "limit"
    assert len(adapter.events) == 1
    assert adapter.events[0]["variant"] == "V-INVALID-REQUEST"
    assert adapter.events[0]["rules_version"] is None


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "date,lookback,field",
    [
        ("2026-02-30", 2, "as_of_date"),
        ("2026-9-28", 2, "as_of_date"),
        ("2026-09-28", -1, "look_back_days"),
        ("2026-09-28", True, "look_back_days"),
    ],
)
def test_s3_invalid_date_or_lookback_never_fetches(monkeypatch, adapter, date, lookback, field):
    monkeypatch.setattr(news.yf, "Search", lambda **kwargs: pytest.fail("fetched"))
    with pytest.raises(InvalidRequestError) as error:
        news.get_global_news_yfinance(date, look_back_days=lookback)
    assert error.value.field == field
    assert [event["variant"] for event in adapter.events] == ["V-INVALID-REQUEST"]
    assert adapter.events[0]["rules_version"] is None


def test_s3_zero_limit_skips_vendor(monkeypatch, adapter):
    monkeypatch.setattr(news.yf, "Search", lambda **kwargs: pytest.fail("fetched"))

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Deterministic semantic evaluation report for the approved O5 case set.

This runs the *real* approved O5 tests (through the real production entry
``get_global_news_yfinance``) for a versioned, fixed case set, and emits a
machine-readable report with per-case IDs and results against a 100% safety
threshold. It fails nonzero if any required case is missing, errored, skipped,
or failed.

Scope honesty:
- Covers only the deterministic O5 safety cases defined in this file. It does
  NOT validate arbitrary prompt/model changes, and it is not a general
  text-quality evaluator.
- Prompt/model paths *not* covered by these cases are reported explicitly as
  uncovered (see ``COVERED_PATHS`` / ``UNCOVERED``).
- Real test execution is required; pre-filled scores are rejected by design
  (the report is produced only from actual pytest outcomes).

Usage:
    python scripts/semantic_report.py [--json PATH]

Exit codes:
    0  all required cases passed (100% safety threshold met)
    1  at least one required case failed / missing / errored / skipped
    2  execution/internal error
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import subprocess
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from pathlib import Path

# Versioned case set. Each case = a real pytest node executing the real entry.
CASESET_VERSION = "o5-deterministic-v1"
THRESHOLD_PASS_RATE = 1.0  # 100% of required cases

# case_id -> (node_id, description, covered prompt/model path)
CASES: dict[str, tuple[str, str, str]] = {
    "O5-REL-01": (
        "test/offline/test_o5_macro_news_integration.py::test_s4_selected_path_filters_before_slice_and_keeps_fields",
        "relevant macro news selected via real get_global_news_yfinance (filter-before-slice)",
        "tradingagents/dataflows/vendors/yahoo/news.py:get_global_news_yfinance (selector path)",
    ),
    "O5-EMPTY-01": (
        "test/offline/test_o5_macro_news_integration.py::test_s4_t04d_filtered_to_zero_is_not_upstream_empty",
        "irrelevant candidates filtered to zero (distinct from upstream-empty)",
        "get_global_news_yfinance (filtered-empty path)",
    ),
    "O5-EMPTY-02": (
        "test/offline/test_o5_macro_news_integration.py::test_s4_t04d_all_irrelevant_uses_the_all_irrelevant_enum_member",
        "all-irrelevant -> ALL_IRRELEVANT exact enum member",
        "get_global_news_yfinance (ALL_IRRELEVANT path)",
    ),
    "O5-UNAVAIL-01": (
        "test/offline/test_o5_macro_news_integration.py::test_s4_filter_unavailable_text_is_distinct_from_filtered_empty",
        "filter unavailable -> suppression, no unvalidated publication",
        "get_global_news_yfinance (FILTER_UNAVAILABLE path)",
    ),
    "O5-LIMIT0-01": (
        "test/offline/test_o5_macro_news_integration.py::test_s3_zero_limit_skips_vendor",
        "limit=0 -> zero vendor calls",
        "get_global_news_yfinance (LIMIT_ZERO short-circuit)",
    ),
}

# Prompt/model paths relevant to semantic policy but NOT covered by this fixed set.
UNCOVERED = [
    "Arbitrary prompt edits (e.g. analyst/PM system prompts) — no fixed quality case in this set",
    "Model/provider swaps — not exercised by the deterministic O5 cases",
    "Non-deterministic text-quality scoring — no calibrated evaluator/threshold in this set",
    "LLM tier routing / reasoning effort changes — out of scope for this set",
]

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def run_cases(junit_path: Path) -> int:
    node_ids = [c[0] for c in CASES.values()]
    cmd = [
        sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "-q", "-p", "no:cacheprovider",
        f"--junitxml={junit_path}", *node_ids,
    ]
    proc = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=REPO_ROOT)
    return proc.returncode


def parse_junit(junit_path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Map node id -> outcome ('passed'|'failed'|'error'|'skipped')."""
    outcomes: dict[str, str] = {}
    if not junit_path.is_file():
        return outcomes
    tree = ET.parse(junit_path)
    for tc in tree.iter("testcase"):
        # junit classname + name; reconstruct approx node id by matching suffix
        name = tc.get("name", "")
        outcome = "passed"
        for child in tc:
            tag = child.tag
            if tag in ("failure",):
                outcome = "failed"
            elif tag in ("error",):
                outcome = "error"
            elif tag in ("skipped",):
                outcome = "skipped"
        outcomes[name] = outcome
    return outcomes


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--json", type=Path, default=Path("semantic-report.json"))
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    if not (REPO_ROOT / "test/offline/test_o5_macro_news_integration.py").is_file():
        print("ERROR: O5 integration test file not present; cannot run authorized cases.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    junit = REPO_ROOT / "semantic-junit.xml"
    rc = run_cases(junit)
    junit_outcomes = parse_junit(junit)

    results = []
    required_failed = []
    for case_id, (node_id, desc, path) in CASES.items():
        test_name = node_id.rsplit("::", 1)[-1]
        outcome = junit_outcomes.get(test_name, "missing")
        ok = outcome == "passed"
        results.append({
            "case_id": case_id, "node_id": node_id, "covered_path": path,
            "description": desc, "outcome": outcome, "pass": ok,
        })
        if not ok:
            required_failed.append(case_id)

    passed = sum(1 for r in results if r["pass"])
    total = len(results)
    rate = passed / total if total else 0.0
    threshold_met = (rate >= THRESHOLD_PASS_RATE) and not required_failed

    report = {
        "caseset_version": CASESET_VERSION,
        "threshold_pass_rate": THRESHOLD_PASS_RATE,
        "results": results,
        "passed": passed,
        "total": total,
        "pass_rate": rate,
        "required_failed": required_failed,
        "threshold_met": threshold_met,
        "covered_paths": [c[2] for c in CASES.values()],
        "uncovered_changes": UNCOVERED,
        "note": "Deterministic O5 safety cases only; not a general prompt/model quality evaluator.",
    }
    args.json.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")

    print(f"semantic case set {CASESET_VERSION}: {passed}/{total} passed "
          f"(threshold {THRESHOLD_PASS_RATE:.0%})")
    for r in results:
        print(f"  [{'PASS' if r['pass'] else 'FAIL'}] {r['case_id']} {r['node_id']} -> {r['outcome']}")
    for u in UNCOVERED:
        print(f"  [UNCOVERED] {u}")

    if not threshold_met:
        print(f"SEMANTIC FAILED: required cases failed/missing: {required_failed}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if rc not in (0,):
        # pytest reported failure but our threshold logic passed -> inconsistency
        print(f"SEMANTIC FAILED: pytest exit {rc} despite threshold check", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print("SEMANTIC OK: all required deterministic O5 cases passed")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
